fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.

feat(demos): themes-and-color-studio flagship (rich-demos-l2x.3) (#34)

* feat(demos): themes-and-color-studio flagship — folds 4 demos, burns down 23 allowlist entries (rich-demos-l2x.3)

One non-interactive flagship demo replaces four overlapping ones
(rich-themes, rich-themes-transposed, rich-theme-designer, rich-colors).
[LAW:no-mode-explosion] [LAW:one-source-of-truth]

# Shape

Single file orchestrating eight sections as data, each exercising a layer
of the public API:

  1. Color values — ColorRgba, parseRgbHex/parseRgbaHex, blendRgb,
     compositeOver, ColorParseError.
  2. ColorSpec — factories (parse/fromAnsi/fromRgba/fromRgb/default),
     ColorDepth enum, downgrade across STANDARD_TABLE / EIGHT_BIT_TABLE /
     WINDOWS_TABLE, ANSI_COLOR_NAMES lookups.
  3. System detection — detectColorSystem with DetectColorOptions over
     four env fixtures, resolveColorSystem spec strings.
  4. Theme registry — listThemePalettes / getThemePalette /
     getThemeBaseColors walking every bundled theme, plus the raw
     THEMES / ThemePaletteData / ThemeName / ThemeBaseColors via the
     ./themes/data and ./themes/registry subpaths.
  5. PaletteResolver — bare / modifier / alpha / auto / composed specs
     against gruvbox; buildPalette + BaseColors to show derived
     primary-muted / text-primary / on-primary vars.
  6. TerminalTheme constants — all 23 bundled constants in one catalog
     row each (DEFAULT, SVG_EXPORT, MONOKAI, NORD, GRUVBOX, DRACULA,
     TOKYO_NIGHT, FLEXOKI, CYBERPUNK, CATPPUCCIN_*, SOLARIZED_*,
     ROSE_PINE*, ATOM_ONE_*, TEXTUAL_*).
  7. OKLCH transposition — Oklch / IDENTITY / INVERT_LIGHTNESS /
     isIdentityKey, transposePalette hue circle + chroma sweep + invert,
     themeKeyForRoot aiming a tonic at 200°, ANCHORED_ROOTS / isAnchored
     visibly locking error/success/warning hue.
  8. WCAG contrast — relativeLuminance / contrastRatio / contrastFor /
     ensureContrast across a gruvbox matrix plus three hard cases where
     ensureContrast slides L from <2:1 up to ≥4.5:1 while preserving hue.

[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] SECTIONS is the order; the orchestrator
loops over a function array. Section internals iterate data tables
(theme catalogs, spec lists, env fixtures) so adding a row never
requires editing logic.

[LAW:single-enforcer] bgFgStyle is the only place the demo flattens
alpha + applies ensureContrast(4.5). Every styled cell goes through it.

# Folded

- examples/rich-themes/                    (palette walk)
- examples/rich-themes-transposed/         (hue circle, chroma, invert)
- examples/rich-theme-designer/            (interactive picker)
- examples/rich-colors/                    (interactive color browser)

The interactive widget-based demos (theme-designer, colors) intentionally
do not get a TUI replacement here — their widget references belong to
widgets-playground (rich-demos-l2x.5) and the actual coverage they
provided for color/theme APIs is now satisfied non-interactively. The
flagship's spec contract was 'exercises every mapped API,' not 'preserves
every UX.' [feedback:no-legacy-code]

# Allowlist burn-down (23 entries → 0)

ANCHORED_ROOTS, BaseColors, ColorTable, DetectColorOptions,
EIGHT_BIT_TABLE, Oklch, ResolveContext, TEXTUAL_ANSI, TEXTUAL_DARK,
TEXTUAL_LIGHT, THEMES, ThemeBaseColors, ThemeName, ThemePaletteData,
buildPalette, detectColorSystem, getThemeBaseColors, isAnchored,
isIdentityKey, parseRgbaHex, relativeLuminance, resolveColorSystem,
themeKeyForRoot.

Verified via test/coverage/coverage.test.ts: removing the entries with
the demo in place leaves the verifier green; removing any one without a
matching reference would fail loudly.

# Test cleanup

test/examples/transpose-explore.test.ts is removed alongside its
demo — it tested the explorer's internal model (reduce, previewCells,
renderFrame, framesToSegments, appMock, renderShowcase), not the public
API. [LAW:behavior-not-structure] Public-API behavior is covered by
test/themes/transpose.test.ts, test/themes/colorMath.test.ts, and
test/core/oklch.test.ts.

# npm script

  npm run themes-and-color-studio                # terminal
  EXPORT_HTML=out.html npm run themes-and-color-studio  # +HTML export

Old scripts removed: colors, theme-designer, themes, themes:transposed,
themes:explore.

Closes rich-demos-l2x.3.

* docs(demos): address PR-34 review — derive count, fix SVG/section-7 labels, sync README

Four Copilot findings, three architectural in shape:

- Section 6's title hard-coded '19 bundled themes' against a 23-entry
  catalog. Fixed at the right level: hoist TERMINAL_THEME_CATALOG to
  module scope and derive the count from .length so the title and data
  cannot disagree. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] Adding a theme bumps the
  printed count automatically — the prose tracks the data.

- Section 6's SVG_EXPORT_THEME blurb claimed it was 'paper-on-ink' and
  used a 'light substrate', but the data file declares dark:true with
  bg=#292929 (a near-black, not light). Rewrote the description to
  match the actual theme: both DEFAULT and SVG_EXPORT are dark; SVG
  lifts off pure black so an embedded SVG substrate is distinguishable
  from a possible host-page background. (Pure inverted claim → load-
  bearing-false comment; fix is to make the description honest, not
  preserve the wrong framing.)

- Section 7's printed sub-labels (7a/7b/7c/7d) were correct, but the
  source comments numbered the five blocks 7a–7e (counting the
  introductory Oklch-round-trip block). Re-numbered the comments to
  match the printed labels: the intro is now labelled 'Setup' and the
  four labeled sub-demos line up 7a/7b/7c/7d in both source and output.

- README still listed 'npm run colors' and carried a full
  '### rich-colors' demo section for a demo this PR removed. Replaced
  the demo-command entry with 'npm run themes-and-color-studio' and
  rewrote the section to describe the new flagship (eight sub-sections,
  EXPORT_HTML usage, the actual modules/symbols exercised). Also
  dropped two now-stale 'Not yet exercised' entries that proposed
  features for the deleted rich-colors demo and that this flagship now
  covers directly (Color downgrading, theme switcher hooks).

npm run lint clean; coverage verifier (test/coverage/coverage.test.ts)
remains green — the themes-and-color-studio burn-down block stays
empty because every owned export is still referenced by the demo.

* docs(demos): address PR-34 round-2 review — derive every prose count from data

Three more Copilot findings, all the same shape as round 1's first finding:
prose-count drift. The fix isn't 'update the number' — it's to design the
shape so the number cannot drift in the first place. [LAW:one-source-of-truth]

The reported findings:
- Section 2 blurb claimed downgrade uses 'one of three ColorTables:
  STANDARD/EIGHT_BIT/WINDOWS'. The source explicitly treats WINDOWS as
  unreachable from performDowngrade (it's a *detection* result, not a
  downgrade target). Rewrote the blurb to describe what actually happens:
  downgrade quantizes through STANDARD_TABLE and EIGHT_BIT_TABLE;
  WINDOWS_TABLE is a public LUT for the Windows console palette.
- Section 2 downgrade-walk comment said 'three targets'; the code only
  downgrades to two. Reworded to describe the three *renderings*
  (truecolor original + two quantization steps) accurately.
- Section 3 fixture comment said 'Three deterministic env fixtures' but
  the cases array has four. Dropped the count and replaced with the WHY
  (each fixture exercises a specific detection branch).

Proactive sweep — same anti-pattern, other instances:
- 'blendRgb — five steps' → 'steps' (count dropped; the array is the
  truth).
- 'Six is the sweet spot ... at 120 cells' (SEMANTIC_VARS comment) →
  'Sized to fit on one line of the configured console width' (drops both
  the hardcoded 6 and the hardcoded 120).
- '7a. Hue circle — six rotations' (printed + comment) → derived from
  HUE_ROTATIONS.length, so adding or removing a rotation updates the
  printed count automatically. Same fix as round 1's catalog.length.
- '7b. Chroma sweep — five saturation levels' → derived from
  CHROMA_SCALES.length, same shape.

After this pass there are no hand-maintained counts in prose anywhere
in this file; every numeric mention in section titles either describes
a real domain quantity (degrees, ratios, indices in standard ANSI) or
is derived from the data it claims to count.

npm run lint clean; test/coverage/coverage.test.ts green.

* docs(demos): address PR-34 round-3 review — exhaustive parse-outcome match + honest demo list

Two moderate findings, both about loud-failure boundaries [LAW:no-silent-fallbacks]:

- Section 1's parse-error assertion only printed a diagnostic *if* parse
  threw — so a regression that made parse silently return some default
  would have emitted nothing and the demo would have appeared to pass.
  Replaced the try/catch with a discriminated-union ParseOutcome (correct
  | wrong-type | no-throw) computed once and matched into exactly one
  printed line, so every possible outcome surfaces a diagnostic. The
  type forbids the 'silent on no-throw' case at compile time rather
  than at vibes. [LAW:types-are-the-program] The exhaustive match is
  the proof: any new ParseOutcome variant would force a new diagnostic
  branch before the code compiles.

- README "## Demos" claimed 'Two interactive TUI demos' but package.json
  actually defines seven other demo scripts (rich-config / dropdown-demo /
  rich-dash / rich-template-bindings / rich-strip / rich-markup-plugins /
  themes-and-color-studio). Restructured the section to list every demo
  script that exists, grouped by 'detailed below', 'other interactive',
  and 'non-interactive transcripts', with one-line summaries. The note
  'the full set of available npm scripts is the authoritative list' makes
  the relationship explicit: package.json is the canonical source, the
  README is a curated view. [LAW:one-source-of-truth]

npm run lint clean; coverage verifier green; the new parse-outcome
match preserves the original green ✓ output on the happy path.
